INTU.thesis_one_line: Tax and small-business software platform still growing double digits, priced as if growth stalls forever, despite a costly recent restructuring.
kill_criteria: TurboTax or Credit Karma segment revenue growth turns negative for 2 consecutive quarters
Non-GAAP operating margin compresses >300bps YoY for 2 consecutive quarters
A third major workforce restructuring (>5% of headcount) announced within 24 months of the May-2026 cut
Full-year revenue or non-GAAP EPS guidance is cut (vs. the prior range) at any of the next 4 quarterly releases
Net debt/EBITDA rises above 1.5x via debt-funded M&A
key_adverse_facts: Second major workforce restructuring in 24 months (Jul-2024 ~1,800; May-2026 ~3,000, 17% of staff), with $300-340M restructuring charge

CEO gave contradictory public rationale for the May-2026 cut: told employees it was to become 'leaner, more focused', told CNBC 'none of it had to do with AI', while investor materials tout AI as the growth driver

FTC consent order (since Jan-2024) permanently bars TurboTax 'free' advertising claims without disclosing the ~1/3 qualification rate; company did not renew IRS Free File Program participation for 2026

[DVH1 2026-10-06] replaces the original: SBC is 9.6% of FY26 revenue ($2,056M). From 1 Aug 2026 Intuit no longer excludes SBC from non-GAAP measures; the FY27 non-GAAP EPS guide ($22.88-23.12) includes a $5.81 SBC cost, so FY26 non-GAAP $24.27 and the FY27 guide are on different bases.
Long-run AI/free-filing disintermediation risk to TurboTax/Credit Karma is unconfirmed but not resolved (triage-flagged, monitored not verified this quarter)
data_conflicts: None material vs V1 (no V1 row exists for INTU). Triage's cited 11.3x NTM P/E is broadly consistent with this dossier's own 12.0x non-GAAP / 13.6x GAAP forward multiples (small difference from EPS-base timing).
INTU.confidence_in_thesis: medium - strong fundamentals and a reverse DCF implying near-zero perpetual growth support the valuation case, but the AI-disintermediation risk to the core tax franchise and the restructuring/credibility issue are genuine unresolved unknowns, not yet falsified either way

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: [DVH1 2026-10-06] original single-stage perpetuity (WACC 9.5%) implied -1.3% (+1.1% after SBC). Restated on programme ten-year model (rf 5.17%, ERP 4.14%, Blume beta 0.98, WACC about 8.8%, 3% terminal; unlevered FCF after SBC and interest income about $6.46bn; EV $76.7bn): about -2.2%/yr vs a base of about 15% EPS growth. implied_vs_base stays 'below', more strongly. FY26 FCF is $8.617B (capex $221M). No V1 row exists.

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: 3yr exit-multiple model off non-GAAP EPS ($24.27 TTM): bear = ~0%/yr EPS growth, multiple compresses to 8x (AI-disintermediation case); base = ~15%/yr EPS growth (below the FY27 guide's 23-24%), multiple holds ~12x (no re-rating); bull = ~22%/yr EPS growth, multiple re-rates to 17x (partial recovery toward historical premium); all include ~3yrs of cumulative dividends.

MS.thesis_one_line: Wall Street's top wealth manager and investment bank just posted record profits, but the price already assumes today's boom-time returns last indefinitely.
kill_criteria: ROTCE falls below 18% for 2 consecutive quarters
Wealth Management net new assets fall below $50B/quarter for 2 consecutive quarters
A new SEC/DOJ/FINRA enforcement action or fine >$100M is announced
Provision for credit losses in Institutional Securities exceeds $300M in a single quarter without a matching one-off disclosed cause
key_adverse_facts: Q2 2026 record results were driven heavily by trading (Equity net revenues +69% YoY), which the company itself attributes to favorable market conditions rather than structural share gain - inherently cyclical
Standardized CET1 (14.8% vs 15.0% YoY) and Tier 1 leverage (6.0% vs 6.8% YoY) are both declining while quarterly buybacks accelerated from $1.0B to $1.5B
Provision for credit losses driven partly by growth in corporate loans and commercial real estate lending - a credit-quality watch item, not yet a deterioration signal

Pattern of recent regulatory settlements: $249.4M DOJ/SEC block-trading settlement (Jan-2024) and $15M SEC fine for failing to monitor advisor account transfers that enabled misappropriation (Dec-2024)
data_conflicts: None vs V1 (no V1 row exists for MS). Triage's ~14.6x forward multiple is broadly consistent with this dossier's own 15.9x TTM P/E.
MS.confidence_in_thesis: medium - the wealth-management re-mix and capital return are real and well-documented, but the reverse-ROTCE valuation math showing the price requires sustaining a just-posted cyclical-peak ROTCE is a clear, quantified reservation

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for MS, so there is nothing to reconcile against; this is the analyst's own reverse valuation. Solving P/TBV=(ROTCE-g)/(COE-g) at the current 3.69x P/TBV implies the market needs Morgan Stanley to sustain roughly the 26% ROTCE it just posted this quarter in perpetuity, above a more conservative normalized through-cycle base case (historically discussed nearer 20%), so implied growth/return is above the analyst's base case.

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: 3yr exit-P/E model off TTM EPS ($12.37): bear = trading/IB normalizes, EPS reverts to ~$11/yr, P/E compresses to 12x; base = EPS grows modestly to ~$13.5/yr (partial trading normalization offset by WM growth), P/E ~15x (near current); bull = cycle stays hot, EPS ~$16/yr, P/E re-rates to 17x on sustained >25% ROTCE; all include ~3yrs of cumulative dividends.

NUE.thesis_one_line: America's largest steelmaker is riding record tariff-boosted prices and shipments, but the stock is priced as if today's unusually high profits are permanent.
kill_criteria: Steel-mill average selling price falls below $800/ton for 2 consecutive quarters
Quarterly diluted EPS falls back below $2.00 for 2 consecutive quarters
Section 232 steel tariffs are repealed or substantially weakened
The 213-consecutive-quarter dividend streak is broken or a previously-declared increase is skipped
key_adverse_facts: Quarterly diluted EPS swung from a $0.67 trough (Q1 2025) to $5.04 (Q2 2026), a >7x move in five quarters - a textbook commodity-cycle profile, not a compounding growth trajectory
FCF yield on EV is only ~2.6% (TTM FCF $1.583B) despite the earnings surge, because Nucor is mid-way through a large multi-year capacity-expansion capex program (~$1.1-1.3B/quarter)
Tariff-dependent pricing is a policy moat, not a competitive one; a trade-policy reversal is a named, real risk to the current pricing premium

Nucor's own press releases give only qualitative directional guidance (no point EPS/revenue range); the $5.55-5.65 Q3 2026 EPS figure circulating in the press was not found in the primary 8-K exhibit and is sourced to secondary/analyst commentary
data_conflicts: V1's reverse-DCF sub-model for NUE was explicitly suppressed because D&A was unavailable and treated as 0. The primary 10-Q cash-flow statement reports TTM Depreciation of $1,261M (~3.5% of TTM revenue), which is readily available and not zero - a real data gap in V1's pipeline, now sourced and used in this dossier's own reverse DCF (Section 7). Using the corrected D&A, a single-stage FCFF reverse DCF implies ~+6.2%/yr perpetual growth, which taken at face value looks less alarming than V1's -10.5%/yr base-case return; the dossier reconciles this by noting the FCFF calc takes a cyclically elevated TTM EBIT margin as the sustainable base, which is not appropriate for a commodity steelmaker, and adopts V1's margin-mean-reversion framework as the more credible lens.
NUE.confidence_in_thesis: medium - balance sheet and capital-return discipline are unambiguously strong, but whether current steel pricing/shipment levels are a durable plateau or a cyclical peak is genuinely uncertain and policy-dependent

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: Agrees directionally with V1's excessive verdict. V1's own reverse-DCF sub-model was suppressed due to a missing D&A input; this dossier sourced the real TTM D&A (~$1.26B) from the 10-Q and found a corrected single-stage FCFF reverse DCF implies only ~+6.2%/yr perpetual growth, which looks less demanding than V1's EPS-scenario base case. The reconciliation is that the FCFF calc uses TTM EBIT margin (~11.8%) as the sustainable base, but that margin is itself a tariff/pricing-cycle high for a commodity steelmaker; V1's margin-mean-reversion framework is the more appropriate lens, so the final conclusion (price is priced for more than a prudent normalized-margin base case delivers) is unchanged.

scenario_returns_3y.scenario_basis: Adopted directly from V1's own EPS-scenario/exit-multiple model (v1_valuation.json NUE.scenarios), not re-derived, since this dossier's disagreement with V1 is about the FCFF sub-model only (Section 7) and it independently agrees with V1's margin-mean-reversion-based bear/base/bull framework for this cyclical commodity producer.
